Arca di Noah

An animal shelter in Sicily. I was its Marketing & Communication Manager from August 2025 to February 2026, working remotely, and led the move from informative posts to video-first storytelling.

In 90 days, with no paid ads, the account reached 545K people and its Reels were watched 1.1M times.

53 Reels, 12K shares and 2.6K saves between 17 November 2025 and 15 February 2026. Followers grew by 600% to 1,400, and social media inquiries went from almost none to 10 qualified adoption applications in a single month.

Simple on purpose.

The audience was mostly Italian, with a lot of older followers and mums. They didn’t want fast cuts and effects. They wanted clear text on screen, a bit of humour and honest updates about the dogs.

So that’s what I made. These videos aren’t built to impress other editors; they’re built for the people who actually adopt.

Captions are in Italian, so each piece has a short English summary.

Reel, 6 January 2026

“I can’t adopt a dog, I don’t work from home…”

Starts from the excuse people give most often, in their own words, and answers it: you don’t need a perfect home, just the willingness to give a dog a chance.

666K views169K accounts reached, 768 shares, 10K likes, 11.1 s average watch time

Reel, 15 January 2026, humour

“Do you have purebred dogs for adoption?” Part 1

Turns a question the shelter is tired of hearing into a joke: no purebreds, only “limited editions” and “prototypes never put on the market”. People sent it to their friends.

297K views214K accounts reached, 3.6K shares, 15K likes, 666 comments

Reel, 23 January 2026, humour

“Do you have purebred dogs for adoption?” Part 2

Same joke, new punchline: a “collection of unique pieces” you won’t find at any breeder. Making it a series gave followers a reason to come back for the next one.

121K views93K accounts reached, 1.5K shares, 7.1K likes, 342 comments

Urgent adoption: Nuvola

Built around one line, “not a plush toy: a puppy who already knows what abandonment is”. Publishing it as a collaboration and cross-posting to Facebook took it beyond the shelter’s own followers.

Reel, 31 December 2025, longer narrative

“Sofia was left one step from the finish line”

Sofia’s adoption was cancelled the night before. No polish, just the truth told to the people who had followed her story. It held attention longer than anything else here.

Sottosuono

Underground electronic music collective, co-founded in Bologna, now relaunching in Amsterdam.

Five nights so far, usually 60 to 100 people each. I curate the line-ups, play vinyl, and promote every event through Instagram, flyers, broadcasts and word of mouth.

Here the audience wants the opposite of the shelter’s: texture, mood and a bit of mystery. The visual language is mirrored ink, like a Rorschach test, so every flyer asks the same question as the blot at the top of this page.

With AI

Image tools help me get an idea in front of people fast. Everything in this section uses AI-generated imagery.

I use AI the way I’d use a moodboard or a quick shoot: to test a direction before anyone spends real time or money on it. I write the brief, direct the generations and keep going until the result fits the audience, not until it looks impressive.

Winter blues, for students

An Instagram carousel from a health communication intervention at the University of Amsterdam, aimed at students who feel low every winter but don’t think it’s serious enough to ask for help.

It opens with a question instead of a diagnosis, lets people recognise themselves in a checklist, and then takes away the “depressed enough” barrier. The halftone illustrations are AI-generated; the red and white keep it calm without feeling clinical.

Trémont

Concept images for a friend’s watch brand. The goal was a quiet, premium feel for an older, design-minded buyer: warm, natural light, real skin, leather and old paint, nothing shiny or loud, and the same watch kept consistent from shot to shot, by day and by night.

The brand went another way, so these were never published.
